raw_text: The Congress of Vienna was convened in 1814 to reconstruct Europe after the Napoleonic Wars. Prince Klemens von Metternich, the Austrian foreign minister, played a central role in the negotiations. The Congress was attended by representatives from Austria, Prussia, Russia, and Great Britain. Tsar Alexander I of Russia sought to expand Russian influence across the continent. The resulting Concert of Europe established a balance of power that lasted for decades. Baron Karl vom Stein, a Prussian statesman, also participated in early discussions but died before the Congress concluded. The Treaty of Paris was signed on May 30, 1814, preceding the Congress. Metternich later became the dominant figure in European diplomacy, championing conservatism against nationalist and liberal movements.
